title.en: Hackers steal sensitive data from UK Department for Education and police
title.zh: 黑客从英国教育部和警方窃取敏感数据

summary.en: Details of parents and staff, including email addresses and phone numbers, are among data taken by cybercriminals The Department for Education and a police database have been targeted by a cyber-attack, exposing more than 740,000 pieces of data. Details of government officials,...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Department for Education and a police database have been targeted by a cyber-attack, exposing more than 740,000 pieces of data.

Details of government officials, senior school leaders, university staff, police officers and members of the public have been taken by hackers.

Just over 600,000 lines of data have been stolen from the DfE’s help-desk portal. They show parent and staff contacts including full names, email addresses, phone numbers and job titles, according to a “leak” website set up by the hackers.

A smaller package of similar data has been taken from the department’s Turing portal, which manages a scheme for students studying abroad.

The hackers have also breached the police national legal database (PNLD), which provides legal assistance to UK police forces. The cybercriminals claimed to have taken 135,000 pieces of data.

The PNLD said the details taken related to “police officers and those working in criminal justice including their name, the force or organisation they work for and their work email address”.

Some names and addresses of members of the public who had previously submitted a question to the Ask the Police service had also been taken. It said the database did not hold confidential victim, witness or offender information.

While embarrassing, the breach of the police legal database is not thought to be serious.

A previously unknown hacking gang calling itself ExfilSquad claimed it had carried out the attack and posted samples of the data on its leak site, a typical gambit for cybercriminals seeking money for the information they have stolen.

The hackers are demanding a payment from the DfE and PNLD in exchange for not posting all the data, according to screen grabs seen by the Guardian.

The message states that only a small sample of data has been posted for now but indicates that all of it will be uploaded if the DfE, PNLD and other hacking victims do not make an unspecified payment.

“The payment we request of you is simply a rounding error compared to the litigation costs of your data leaking. Be smart and just pay,” said the gang.

The message is apparently directed at 14 hacking victims including the DfE. The list of alleged victims includes a UK university that has been contacted by the Guardian.

Sophos, a cybersecurity company that provided the screenshots, said the data samples appeared to be legitimate. It added that an account on the social media platform X apparently belonging to the group had been suspended but had been illustrated by a picture of a cybersecurity researcher who had been targeted before by members of the Com , a sprawling ecosystem of native English-speaking hackers.

body.zh: 教育部和警方数据库遭到网络攻击，超过 74 万条数据被泄露。 政府官员、学校高级领导、大学工作人员、警察和公众的详细信息已被黑客窃取。 DfE 服务台门户网站中超过 600,000 行数据被盗。根据黑客建立的一个“泄露”网站，这些信息显示了家长和员工的联系方式，包括全名、电子邮件地址、电话号码和职位。 从该部门的图灵门户网站中获取了一小部分类似数据，该门户网站管理着一项针对出国留学的学生的计划。 黑客还入侵了警察国家法律数据库（PNLD），该数据库为英国警察部队提供法律援助。网络犯罪分子声称窃取了 135,000 条数据。 PNLD 表示，所获取的详细信息涉及“警察和刑事司法工作人员，包括他们的姓名、他们工作的部队或组织以及他们的工作电子邮件地址”。 之前向“询问警察”服务部门提交问题的一些公众的姓名和地址也被记录下来。它说该数据库不保存受害人、证人或罪犯的机密信息。 虽然令人尴尬，但警方法律数据库的泄露被认为并不严重。 一个自称 ExfilSquad 的此前不为人知的黑客团伙声称实施了此次攻击，并在其泄露网站上发布了数据样本，这是网络犯罪分子为窃取信息谋取金钱的典型策略。 根据《卫报》看到的屏幕截图，黑客要求 DfE 和 PNLD 付款，以换取不发布所有数据。 该消息指出，目前只发布了一小部分数据样本，但表示如果 DfE、PNLD 和其他黑客受害者不支付未具体说明的付款，所有数据都将被上传。 “与您的数据泄露的诉讼费用相比，我们要求您支付的费用只是四舍五入的误差。聪明点，只需支付即可，”该团伙说。 该消息显然是针对包括 DfE 在内的 14 名黑客受害者。据称受害者名单中包括《卫报》联系的一所英国大学。 提供屏幕截图的网络安全公司 Sophos 表示，这些数据样本似乎是合法的。它还补充说，社交媒体平台 X 上的一个显然属于该组织的帐户已被暂停，但其中有一张网络安全研究人员的照片，该研究人员之前曾被 Com 成员攻击，Com 是一个由英语为母语的黑客组成的庞大生态系统。 然而，据了解，DfE 尚未发现勒索软件（一种锁定...的恶意软件）的证据。

title.en: Saudi Arabia's dilemma as it tries to stay out of US-Iran war
title.zh: 沙特阿拉伯在美伊冲突中力求置身事外的困境

summary.en: Saudi Arabia faces a critical foreign policy decision regarding its conflict with Iran. The kingdom must choose between continuing retaliatory actions as a deterrent or pursuing de-escalation to reduce tensions.
summary.zh: 沙特阿拉伯在与伊朗的冲突中面临一项关键的外交政策抉择。该王国必须选择是继续采取报复行动以示威慑，还是寻求缓和局势以降低紧张。

body.en:
Saudi Arabia is facing a difficult dilemma. Ever since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran on 28 February, the Saudis have largely tried to stay out of it.

But now, after being attacked from three sides, the Saudis have had enough. This week, they carried out joint strikes with the US on Iranian proxy militias in Iraq who they believe have been launching drones at the Kingdom.

For Saudi Arabia the dilemma now is whether to keep on hitting back as a deterrent, or whether to try to de-escalate the situation, perhaps by paying off some of their adversaries.

First, a bit of context. There are broadly two sides in the conflict that has been consuming the Gulf and other parts of the Middle East for five months now.

On one side there is Iran and its Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC). Allied to them are the Houthis in Yemen, a tribal group who took over much of the country in 2014.

Also backed by Iran are the Popular Mobilisation Forces in Iraq, the paramilitary group that has allegedly carried out 30 drone strikes on Saudi Arabia and has now been attacked in return.

Then there is Hezbollah in Lebanon, still a potent force but one that is currently lying low.

On the opposite side of this conflict is the US with its immensely powerful Central Command (Centcom) forces plus - to varying degrees - the Gulf Arab states and Jordan. Israel remains a close US ally but is currently not an active participant in this war.

Iran has most recently been concentrating its drone and missile attacks on Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain, as well as targeting any commercial shipping that tries to slip through the Strait of Hormuz while avoiding Iran's new rules and routing.

The addition of Iraqi militias and the Houthis in Yemen is a relatively new phenomenon and it shows how - without a lasting peace deal between the US and Iran - the region risks becoming ever more embroiled in a widening conflict.

There are a number of reasons why Saudi Arabia is trying not to get sucked into a full-scale conflict.

Its de facto ruler, the relatively young Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman, has embarked the country on a course known as "Vision 2030".

His aim is to diversify the Kingdom away from its dependence on oil revenues and create vibrant, modern, domestic industries that will provide meaningful jobs for the hundreds of thousands of graduates and school leavers pouring onto the job market each year.

Part of Vision 2030 involves attracting foreign investment. Part of it also involves building things like data centres that are vulnerable to attack.

This is not going to work if Saudi Arabia finds itself under an enduring, long-term threat from drones fired across its southern border by the Houthis in Yemen or ballistic missiles fired directly by Iran.

title.en: Anthony Fauci refuses to answer questions during tense US Senate hearing about Covid origins
title.zh: 安东尼·福奇在美国参议院关于新冠病毒起源的紧张听证会上拒绝回答问题

summary.en: Former top US health official Anthony Fauci declined to answer certain questions during a US Senate hearing on Covid origins, citing concerns that Republicans might attempt to manipulate his testimony for perjury charges.
summary.zh: 美国前高级卫生官员安东尼·福奇在美国参议院关于新冠病毒起源的听证会上拒绝回答某些问题，理由是他担心共和党人可能会试图利用他的证词指控他作伪证。

body.en:
Former top US health official Anthony Fauci has refused to answer questions at a tense US Senate hearing on Covid-19, saying he feared Republicans would try to use his testimony to prosecute him for perjury.

He invoked the Fifth Amendment to the US Constitution, which says nobody can be "compelled in any criminal case to be a witness against himself".

Contradicting himself under oath could be legally perilous for him. Fauci noted he had testified about Covid and its origin at several congressional hearings.

Republicans have long accused Fauci of concealing information about the pandemic from the public and lying about its dangers.

He has denied wrongdoing, calling the allegations against him "simply preposterous" in previous testimony to lawmakers.

"Although it pains me to do so because of the respect I have for the legislative branch of government ... under the advice of my attorneys, I will invoke my right under the Fifth Amendment of the constitution to refrain from answering your questions," said, Fauci, 85, former leader of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), at Wednesday's hearing.

Taking the Fifth is not an admission of guilt - it is designed to protect individuals against coercion, mistakes, and unfair shifting of the burden to provide proof of wrongdoing.

While he was granted a pre-emptive pardon by former President Joe Biden, protecting him from federal prosecution for his actions between 2014 to 2025, Fauci could still face charges for anything after that date, including in his actions towards the Senate committee. He could also face state or local charges.

In his statement to the Senate Committee on Homeland Security on Wednesday, Fauci said Republican Senator Rand Paul, who chaired the hearing, had an "obvious obsession" with prosecuting him and that had led Fauci to decline to answer questions.

"The only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something - anything - that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, 'behind bars,'" Fauci said.

Paul, who worked as an eye surgeon before joining Congress, continued questioning Fauci despite his refusal to answer. He repeatedly invited Fauci to "apologise" and said the committee would vote next week on a resolution holding Fauci in contempt of Congress.

Republicans asked Fauci about shifting health guidance, which changed during the pandemic as health officials learned more about the disease. Fauci has previously defended his policy positions.

One of Fauci's lawyers, David Schertler, who was seated next to him, repeatedly tried to interject during Paul's questioning and was removed from the room.

title.en: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina
title.zh: 国际足联对阿根廷启动纪律处分程序

summary.en: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over their behaviour after their World Cup final loss to Spain and throughout the tournament.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Fifa has opened disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over their behaviour after their World Cup final loss to Spain and throughout the tournament.

Last week , the world governing body appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess what happened after the final whistle at the New York New Jersey Stadium, with multiple Argentina players and backroom staff involved in altercations with Spain players following their 1-0 loss in July.

On the recommendation of the prosecutor, Fifa will investigate Argentina players Nahuel Molina (two counts) and Leandro Paredes (three counts), and Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala (one count) for alleged assault under article 14 of Fifa's disciplinary code.

Molina may also face disciplinary action for one count of alleged unsporting behaviour under article 14.

Team-mate Thiago Almada and Spain midfielder Gavi are also accused of the same breach.

Under Fifa's disciplinary code, players and officials face at least a one-match suspension for unsportsmanlike conduct and at least three matches for assault.

The Argentinian Football Association is facing disciplinary proceedings for potential breaches across multiple matches, including using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature (article 13), team misconduct (article 14), discrimination and racist abuse (article 15), and breaching order and security at matches (article 17).

The latter relates to discriminatory chants and gestures, late kick-offs, the team and spectators displaying inappropriate messages, and spectators throwing objects.

Argentina's players celebrated their semi-final win over England with a banner in support of their country's claim to the Falkland Islands . It read "Las Malvinas son Argentinas", which translates as "The Falklands are Argentine".
body.zh: 国际足联已针对阿根廷在世界杯决赛输给西班牙后以及整个赛事期间的行为展开纪律处分。 上周，世界管理机构任命了一名纪律和道德检察官来评估纽约新泽西体育场终场哨响后发生的情况，在七月份0-1输给西班牙队后，多名阿根廷球员和幕后工作人员与西班牙球员发生了争执。 根据检察官的建议，国际足联将根据国际足联纪律守则第14条对阿根廷球员纳韦尔·莫利纳（两项罪名）和莱昂德罗·帕雷德斯（三项罪名）以及阿根廷助理教练罗伯托·阿亚拉（一项罪名）进行调查。 根据第 14 条，莫利纳还可能因一项涉嫌不道德行为而面临纪律处分。 队友蒂亚戈·阿尔马达和西班牙中场加维也被指控犯有同样的违规行为。 根据国际足联的纪律守则，球员和官员若有违反体育道德的行为，将面临至少一场停赛，若有袭击行为，将面临至少三场比赛的处罚。 阿根廷足协正因多场比赛中的潜在违规行为面临纪律处分，包括利用体育赛事进行非体育性质的示威（第 13 条）、球队不当行为（第 14 条）、歧视和种族主义辱骂（第 15 条）以及违反比赛秩序和安全（第 17 条）。 后者涉及歧视性口号和手势、开球延迟、球队和观众展示不当信息以及观众投掷物体。 阿根廷球员庆祝半决赛战胜英格兰时，举起了支持阿根廷对福克兰群岛拥有主权的横幅。上面写着“Las Malvinas son Argentinas”，翻译过来就是“福克兰群岛是阿根廷的”。

title.en: Four women accuse Jared Leto of criminal sexual conduct
title.zh: 四名女性指控杰瑞德·莱托性犯罪行为

summary.en: The actor and musician faces allegations from 10 women in total who say he mistreated them as teenagers.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Four women have accused Oscar-winning actor and Thirty Seconds to Mars frontman Jared Leto of criminal sexual conduct, with the alleged offences having taken place when they were teenagers.

One of the women says she was sexually assaulted in a motel bathroom when she was 17. Another says the Hollywood star threatened her with sexual assault when she was 19, and had been unexpectedly left alone with him in a hotel room.

A third describes how she had under-age sex with the star in California when she was 17 - which would be classified as statutory rape. Leto "shrugged off" a conversation about the age of consent being 18 in the US state, she says.

The fourth woman describes being groomed by Leto, saying he abused his celebrity status by making repeated sexually explicit phone calls to her when she was 16. On at least one occasion, she says he suggested they should have sex.

She was subsequently sent a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) to prevent her from talking about her relationship with Leto, which the BBC has seen. However, she refused to sign.

Four further women also say they received strange and often very sexual phone calls from Leto when they were younger.

Another woman says, when she was 14, he instructed a security guard to take her backstage at a music festival after having made a lewd comment about her chest during an autograph-signing. The girl's mother confronted Leto, but he repeated the comment, it is alleged.

In total, 10 women have spoken to the BBC documentary - Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret - with nine of them sharing their stories publicly for the first time.

All the women say they encountered Leto between 2002 and 2016, when he was in his 30s and 40s. He is now 54.

"This was 25 years ago… he has gotten away with it," says one of his alleged victims.

The BBC has corroborated a number of the women's accounts with friends and family who were told about the encounters with Leto at the time. In some cases, we have also seen pictures and messages that support the women's accounts.

Two men who worked with Leto's band for many years also told the documentary how uncomfortable staff felt about the way Leto would interact with teenage girls, sometimes inviting them backstage to his dressing room or inviting them to the house where he was recording.

Despite repeated attempts to contact Jared Leto before publication, he did not respond to the allegations put to him by the BBC.

In a statement to US media, issued on Wednesday afternoon UK-time, Leto said: "I have never assaulted anyone in my entire life. These claims are absolutely and categorically false."

title.en: France fire crews battle heat as locals tell BBC of fight to save homes
title.zh: 法国消防员在酷热中奋力控制火势

summary.en: Fire crews in France are struggling to contain wildfires in the Gironde region amid 40C heat, with some local residents refusing to evacuate despite the dangers.
summary.zh: 法国吉伦特地区的消防队员在40摄氏度的高温下奋力扑灭野火，尽管存在危险，一些当地居民仍拒绝撤离。

body.en:
The aerial cavalry of three Canadair aircraft flying overhead look as impressive as they sound.

They arrive in formation, before sharply banking over towards the thick plume of black smoke ahead of us.

Their individual payloads of more than 1,000 gallons of water are then dumped onto the flames below.

A succession of helicopters then follows with their own streams of red fire retardant.

As the smoke eases, firefighters then move into the forest on foot to try and contain the latest flare-up.

They are the principal concern for the thousands of crews and volunteers combating the wildfires that have raged here for a week, forcing tens of thousands of residents and tourists to flee.

As temperatures peak at around 40C, fires restarting on their own are a constant threat.

After 20 minutes or so, the one we are watching is brought under control, only for another to suddenly emerge on the opposite side of the road.

"Leave now!" shouts an understandably irritable officer as he drives past. The smoke is becoming thicker and more aggressive. Indeed, time to leave.

Such is the vast scale of the infernos ravaging France's south-western Gironde region, that it is not always obvious what direction the smoke is coming from.

It simply descends as you travel west from Bordeaux along empty roads and through deserted villages.

The soil is powder-like and covered in endless pinecones and dried leaves. It explains how the wildfires have spread at the rate they have.

"When [the police] said I had to leave, I said no!" confessed Pierre Alexandre. The epicentre of the fire started in the woodland next to his bungalow.

He shows a picture of him sitting on the roof of his house in the dark. Pierre Alexandre explained it was in fact taken in the afternoon, after he told his wife and daughter to leave.

He gave his 19-year-old son, Clement, the option of staying if he wanted, which he did.

"I told him: 'Be careful because in front of us is a nightmare, we don't know what will happen,'" explained Pierre Alexandre.

His motivation for wanting to protect his home is relatable, but did he really believe he and Clement could stop the wildfires on their own?

For those who are, controlling these wildfires is like witnessing a lethal game of "cat and mouse" or "Whack-a-Mole". An operation of containment rather than cure.

Behind the professionals are an army of volunteers. They drive towards the danger to either deliver water or spray it themselves.

title.en: Iran war: Egypt's difficult balancing act
title.zh: 伊朗战争：埃及艰难的平衡之举

summary.en: The US-Iran war has already had a negative economic impact on Egypt. Now new threats from the Houthi group in Yemen are likely to worsen that. At the same time, Egypt is trying to stay on good terms with all parties.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US-Iran war has already had a negative economic impact on Egypt. Now new threats from the Houthi group in Yemen are likely to worsen that. At the same time, Egypt is trying to stay on good terms with all parties.

The Suez Canal boasts an array of impressive statistics. At 193 kilometers (120 miles) long, the Egyptian waterway is located between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and it saves ships traveling between Europe and Asia approximately 10,700 kilometers. This is why, since it was opened in 1869, the canal has become one of the world's most important trade routes.

However unrest in the Middle East has seen shipping companies increasingly avoid the Suez Canal over the past couple of years. The Houthi rebel group in Yemen has targeted shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, off the coast of Yemen. To get to the Suez Canal, ships must pass the Bab el-Mandeb and the Yemeni coast.

Recently the Houthis have again threatened to block ships passing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and there are fears that the trend to avoid the Suez Canal will accelerate. 

This is a huge problem for Egypt . Fees paid by shipping companies transiting the Suez Canal are an important source of revenue for the country.

According to Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi, Egypt likely lost around $7 billion (€6.15 billion) from a decrease in traffic through the Suez Canal in 2024 alone. The Reuters news agency said that at times, losses could have been as much as $8 million (€7 million) in a month.

This is why the economic consequence of that loss extends well beyond shipping. Egypt has not been impacted by the Iran conflict in a major military way, but it is certainly seeing an economic effect.

"Economically, Egypt is in a very ambivalent situation," says Stefan Lukas, director of German think tank Middle East Minds.

During 2025 and 2026, revenues from canal transits actually went up again, mainly because oil from the Gulf states was transported via Saudi pipelines to the Red Sea and then onwards through the Suez Canal. This was to avoid the Strait of Hormuz, which is being blocked by Iran and the US in turns. But the new threats by the Houthis to block the Bab el-Mandeb Strait could interfere with this alternative route.

It's bad timing for Egypt: Rising energy prices and the International Monetary Fund's reforms are already putting tough limits on Cairo's financial flexibility.

"Higher energy prices have made imports more expensive and driven up inflation," says Hanna Voss, an expert on the region with Germany's Friedrich Ebert Foundation. "The uncertainty in the Red Sea and potential disruptions to the passage through Bab el-Mandeb are jeopardizing Suez Canal revenues."

body.zh: 美伊战争已经对埃及经济产生了负面影响。现在，来自也门胡塞组织的新威胁可能会使情况变得更糟。与此同时，埃及正努力与各方保持良好关系。 苏伊士运河拥有一系列令人印象深刻的统计数据。埃及水道长 193 公里（120 英里），位于地中海和红海之间，往返于欧洲和亚洲之间的船舶可节省约 10,700 公里。这就是为什么自 1869 年开通以来，这条运河已成为世界上最重要的贸易路线之一。 然而，中东的动荡使得航运公司在过去几年中越来越多地避开苏伊士运河。也门胡塞叛乱组织瞄准了也门沿海曼德海峡的航运。要到达苏伊士运河，船只必须经过曼德海峡和也门海岸。 近期胡塞武装再次威胁封锁曼德海峡船只，有人担心避开苏伊士运河的趋势将加速。 这对埃及来说是一个巨大的问题。通过苏伊士运河的航运公司支付的费用是该国的重要收入来源。 据埃及总统阿卜杜勒-法塔赫·塞西称，仅 2024 年，埃及就可能因苏伊士运河交通量减少而损失约 70 亿美元（61.5 亿欧元）。路透社称，有时一个月内的损失可能高达 800 万美元（700 万欧元）。 这就是为什么这种损失的经济后果远远超出了航运范围。 埃及并未受到伊朗冲突的重大军事影响，但它肯定看到了经济影响。 德国智库“中东思想”主任斯特凡·卢卡斯表示：“从经济角度看，埃及的处境非常矛盾。” 2025年和2026年期间，运河过境收入实际上再次增加，主要是因为海湾国家的石油通过沙特管道运输到红海，然后通过苏伊士运河继续运输。这是为了避开被伊朗和美国轮番封锁的霍尔木兹海峡。但胡塞武装威胁封锁曼德海峡，可能会干扰这条替代路线。 对埃及来说，时机不佳：能源价格上涨和国际货币基金组织的改革已经对开罗的金融灵活性施加了严格的限制。 德国弗里德里希·艾伯特基金会的该地区专家汉娜·沃斯表示：“能源价格上涨使得进口产品更加昂贵，并推高了通货膨胀。” “红海的不确定性以及曼德海峡通道的潜在中断正在危及苏伊士运河的收入。” 埃及旅游业、资本流入和汇率……

title.en: How a Ugandan lost 20 years of her life to xenophobia
title.zh: 乌干达人如何因仇外心理而失去 20 年生命

summary.en: After decades of building lives in South Africa, hundreds of African migrants were forced to leave by renewed anti-immigrant tensions. A Ugandan who spent two decades in South Africa shared with DW how she's coping.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
After decades of building lives in South Africa, hundreds of African migrants were forced to leave by renewed anti-immigrant tensions. A Ugandan who spent two decades in South Africa shared with DW how she's coping.

When Winniefred Kabiri boarded a flight from Johannesburg to Kampala, she was leaving behind much more than a country. The Ugandan entrepreneur spent 20 years legally living in South Africa . During that time, she earned two university degrees and a postgraduate qualification, raised her children and established several businesses.

"Initially everything was very successful. I created a life for myself and educated my children," Kabiri told DW.

But as anti-foreigner campaigns intensified in parts of South Africa this year, she no longer felt safe.

Kabiri is among more than 1,100 Ugandans evacuated from South Africa by their government following months of escalating xenophobic tensions, protests and intimidation targeting mostly African migrants. Uganda completed the first phase of its repatriation exercise in July, bringing home 1,102 nationals through six evacuation flights from Johannesburg.

South Africa has experienced recurring outbreaks of xenophobic violence since the late 1990s, with migrants often blamed for unemployment, crime and poor public services. Analysts say persistent inequality and economic frustration have continued to fuel anti-immigrant sentiment for a while, despite evidence that migrants contribute significantly to local economies .

Groups demanding tougher action against migrants organized public demonstrations and campaigns, while reports of intimidation, evictions and sporadic violence heightened fears among foreign communities. Many immigrants interviewed by DW said they felt vulnerable regardless of whether they possessed legal documentation.

For many returnees, like Kabiri, departure meant abandoning years of investment. She left businesses in commodities trading, mining , real estate and perfume manufacturing. She also left behind a professional network built over two decades.

"Obviously, when you are told to leave and you're unprepared, you leave things behind," she said.

Another Ugandan returnee, Mathias Baguma, said he lost a business he spent years developing in Johannesburg. Baguma moved to South Africa in 2017 and later invested in a guesthouse, restaurant and retail operation. During the unrest, he says the property was attacked and looted.

"My business was vandalized. The shop was robbed, the restaurant broken into," he told DW. "I had to run for my life."

title.en: Iran signals gas price hike as fuel crisis looms
title.zh: 伊朗预示汽油价格上涨，燃料危机迫在眉睫

summary.en: Iranian authorities are considering raising gasoline prices to curb consumption, a move that could lead to social unrest as many households are already struggling under significant economic strain.
summary.zh: 伊朗当局正考虑提高汽油价格以抑制消费，此举可能引发社会动荡，因为许多伊朗家庭已面临严重的经济压力。

body.en:
Iranian authorities want to dampen fuel consumption, but a sudden increase in gasoline prices risks social unrest as many Iranian households are already under severe economic pressure.

Iran is moving closer to politically sensitive changes in gasoline pricing as the government struggles with a widening gap between domestic fuel production and consumption, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict with the US .

On July 25, government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani said changes to fuel prices or rationing are "certain and unavoidable," although officials have yet to confirm whether the response will come through new quotas, higher prices or both.

Iran uses a tiered subsidized fuel price system with monthly quotas currently ranging from 1,500 tomans ($0.008) per liter at the lowest rung, to 5,000 tomans ($0.026) at the top. Iranian media have reported the new top rung for gasoline could jump to 10,000 tomans ($0.053) per liter, which would be nearly a 100% increase. The figure has not yet been officially confirmed.

Compared to the rest of the world, gasoline in Iran seems very inexpensive. But after years of sanctions and economic malaise , Iranians are also earning a lot less. Fuel may look exceptionally cheap in dollar terms, but the incomes used to pay for it are asi exceptionally low.

For example, the basic monthly minimum wage in 2026 was set at around 16.6 million tomans, or about $87. Any hike in gas prices comes down hard on households.

The last major sudden increase in fuel prices in November 2019 triggered nationwide protests and one of the bloodiest crackdowns in the history of the Islamic Republic.

This time, the government faces another complication. Iran was already consuming more gasoline than it produced before the US launched the war in February. Damage to fuel infrastructure and restrictions on imports have made that imbalance harder and more expensive to manage.

Iranian officials argue that they need to suppress demand for gasoline with higher rates. But critics say that gasoline is a necessity and higher costs will not dampen demand.

A resident of Karaj, a small city near Tehran, said that said higher gasoline prices would quickly work their way through the economy, making everything more expensive.

"It will cause a chain reaction in the prices of goods and services, and the greatest pressure will ultimately fall on middle and lower-income households," he told DW anonymously for safety reasons.

A car that consumes roughly 12 liters per 100 kilometers (19 miles per gallon) will not suddenly become more efficient because gasoline costs more, he said. Without better vehicles or effective public transport, motorists have few alternatives.

title.en: Lebanon's pilot zone plan: Can it work?
title.zh: 黎巴嫩的试点区计划：能否奏效？

summary.en: The Israeli army has returned "pilot zones" to the Lebanese, a move intended to help end fighting between Hezbollah and Israel and conclude the Israeli occupation. However, both local residents and experts express skepticism about the plan's potential success.
summary.zh: 以色列军队已将所谓的“试点区”交还给黎巴嫩，此举旨在促进真主党与以色列之间的战斗结束，并结束以色列的占领。然而，当地居民和专家对此计划的成功持怀疑态度。

body.en:
The Israeli army has handed so-called "pilot zones" back to the Lebanese, The move is meant to facilitate an end to fighting between Hezbollah and Israel, and to Israeli occupation. But locals and experts are skeptical.

It has been just over a week since the so-called "pilot zone" plan was launched in Lebanon and the gap between the plan's ambitions and the reality on the ground remains stark.

According to the June 26 agreement between Lebanon, the US and Israel, the pilot zone plan is meant to see the Israeli military gradually redeploying out of parts of southern Lebanon it currently controls, which then allows the Lebanese army, or LAF, to move in.

After the armed wing of Lebanon's Hezbollah group fired rockets at Israel in March this year, Israel invaded Lebanon and now occupies a large swathe of the country’s south. The pilot zones are meant to end that. Once the LAF controls the zone, then Hezbollah can supposedly no longer operate from there. And once one zone has been secured, then the next will be actioned.

However there have been a number of troubling incidents already. The Israeli army shot at the vicinity of Lebanese soldiers as they approached one area last week and Israeli demolitions of homes and buildings in Lebanon continue, as do attacks with drones and bombs elsewhere in southern Lebanon.

The Israeli army's behavior jeopardizes the agreement from which the pilot zone plan originates, Lebanese President Joseph Aoun told the UN's human rights chief Volker Türk this week, when the latter visited Lebanon.

Hussein Kamaleddine, an administrative head, or mukhtar, of Srifa, told DW he didn't understand why his village or the village of Froun had been made a pilot zone because Israeli soldiers had never even been stationed there.  

"This is something that was forced upon us," Kamaleddine said. "It still doesn't make sense to us why these villages were considered pilot zones."

Other commentators have pointed out that lack of Israeli presence may be exactly why these towns were chosen as the first pilot zones: They don't directly impact northern Israel's security and it's a kind of soft launch for the plan.

Kamaleddine said he was happy to be back home in Srifa even though, he noted, he was surrounded by rubble. But he credited that homecoming to his community's resilience, not state support.

"Being back in Srifa now feels like a dream," he said. "But it's not thanks to the government. These so-called pilot zones are nothing but a scheme by the US and Israel."

Authorities from the village of Froun sent DW a written statement, expressing similar opinions. The town supported the LAF and that soldiers coming there had "preserved security and stability," they said.

But at the same time, they also completely rejected...
body.zh: 以色列军队已将所谓的“试验区”交还给黎巴嫩，此举旨在促进结束真主党和以色列之间的战斗以及以色列的占领。但当地人和专家对此表示怀疑。 黎巴嫩启动所谓“试验区”计划仅一周多时间，该计划的雄心壮志与当地现实之间的差距仍然巨大。 根据黎巴嫩、美国和以色列6月26日达成的协议，该试验区计划旨在让以色列军队逐步从其目前控制的黎巴嫩南部部分地区重新部署，然后允许黎巴嫩军队（LAF）进入。 今年3月，黎巴嫩真主党武装派别向以色列发射火箭弹后，以色列入侵黎巴嫩，目前占领了该国南部大片地区。试点区旨在结束这种情况。一旦黎巴嫩空军控制了该地区，真主党就不能再在那里开展活动了。一旦确保了一个区域的安全，就会对下一个区域采取行动。 然而，已经发生了一些令人不安的事件。上周，当黎巴嫩士兵接近一个地区时，以色列军队向他们附近开枪，以色列继续拆除黎巴嫩的房屋和建筑物，并用无人机和炸弹袭击黎巴嫩南部其他地方。 黎巴嫩总统约瑟夫·奥恩本周在联合国人权事务高级专员沃尔克·蒂尔克访问黎巴嫩时告诉他，以色列军队的行为危及了试验区计划所依据的协议。 斯里法行政长官侯赛因·卡马莱丁（Hussein Kamaleddine）告诉德国之声，他不明白为什么他的村庄或弗罗恩村被设为试验区，因为以色列士兵从未驻扎在那里。 “这是强加给我们的，”卡玛莱丁说。 “我们仍然不明白为什么这些村庄被视为试点区。” 其他评论员指出，以色列的缺乏可能正是这些城镇被选为首批试验区的原因：它们不会直接影响以色列北部的安全，这是该计划的一种软启动。 卡马丁表示，他很高兴回到斯里法的家，尽管他周围都是瓦砾。但他将这次回归归功于社区的韧性，而不是国家的支持。 “现在回到斯里法感觉就像一场梦，”他说。 “但这不是政府的功劳。这些所谓的试验区只不过是美国和以色列的一个计划。” 弗罗恩村当局向德国之声发出了一份书面声明，表达了类似的观点。他们说，该镇支持黎巴嫩武装部队，来到那里的士兵“维护了安全和稳定”。 但同时，他们也彻底拒绝了……

reflection.en: The effort to return land and facilitate an end to conflict, despite skepticism, reflects a fundamental human longing for peace. Yahweh's word encourages us to pursue peace whenever it is possible, recognizing that true reconciliation often requires persistent effort and a willingness to engage even amidst doubt. This step, however tentative, reminds us of...
reflection.zh: 尽管存在疑虑，归还土地并促进冲突结束的努力，反映了人类对和平的根本渴望。雅伟的话语鼓励我们，只要可能，就尽力与众人和睦相处，认识到真正的和解往往需要持续的努力，并愿意在怀疑中继续参与。这一步，无论多么试探性，都提醒我们持续寻求和平共处的呼召。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: The 'final frontier' of travelling is here. But one ritual is far from over
title.zh: 旅行的“最终前沿”已至，但一项仪式远未结束

summary.en: A test flight successfully completed a 24-hour non-stop journey, marking a significant milestone in long-haul air travel. This achievement prompts questions about the future of traditional stopovers.
summary.zh: 一架测试航班成功完成了24小时不间断飞行，标志着长途航空旅行的一个重要里程碑。这一成就引发了人们对传统中途停留未来走向的思考。

body.en:
A record-breaking test flight lasting more than 24 hours has touched down in France from Melbourne — and experts say Australia could be leading the world on the new technology use.

Qantas' specially adapted Airbus A350-1000ULR landed in France on Tuesday after a marathon 24 hours and 24 minutes in the air, covering 23,057km without stopping — the longest direct flight ever attempted by a commercial aircraft.

The flight is part of a two-month test campaign as part of Qantas' Project Sunrise, which aims to launch the world's longest commercial passenger flight and reshape long-haul travel by offering direct flights from Australia's east coast to London and New York.

The previous record belonged to a Boeing 777-200LR, which flew 21,601.7km from Hong Kong to London in 22 hours and 42 minutes back in 2005.

Qantas has ordered 12 of the modified A350 aircraft, each fitted with an extra 20,000-litre fuel tank and configured to seat 238 passengers.

The first is due for delivery in April 2027, with daily non-stop flights between Sydney and London planned from October that year — turning what was once a five-day journey in 1947 on the old 'Kangaroo Route' into a single hop of 19 to 21 hours, depending on winds and routing.

The airline has said a Sydney-New York route will follow shortly after the launch of the London route.

The test flight's success has cast eyes towards the future of air travel, with some wondering whether stopovers in Singapore, Dubai or Los Angeles may be a thing of the past.

Justin Brownjohn from RMIT University's Aviation Academy says non-stop routes will keep becoming more viable as aircraft range improves and fuel use falls — but that doesn't make them a replacement for one-stop flying.

"Airlines have historically competed on network and frequency, but Project Sunrise competes on time," he said.

"Cutting up to four hours off the journey from Sydney to London and removing the connection entirely is a different product, not an improved version of the existing one.

Brownjohn expects the strongest demand for the ultra-long-haul services to come from business and premium leisure travellers willing to pay more for the time saved — and says the wider effect may be felt most by the Middle Eastern and Asian hub airports that have built their business models around the layover.

Spending over 20 hours in the air also raises real questions about passenger wellbeing.

"Twenty hours is not a longer flight, it is a different physiological event," Brownjohn said. "On this flight comfort has stopped being a luxury feature and become the thing being sold."

title.en: Saudi Arabian forces join US in strikes on Iran-backed militants in Iraq
title.zh: 沙特阿拉伯军队与美国一道打击伊拉克境内伊朗支持的武装分子

summary.en: Saudi Arabian forces have joined the US in conducting military strikes against Iran-backed militants in Iraq. These strikes were carried out in response to recent drone attacks by the militants on US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure.
summary.zh: 沙特阿拉伯军队与美国一道，对伊拉克境内的伊朗支持的武装分子发动了军事打击。此前，这些武装分子曾对美国军队和沙特能源基础设施发动了二十多次无人机袭击。

body.en:
United States and Saudi Arabian warplanes carried out strikes on Wednesday against Iran-backed militants in Iraq who launched more than two dozen drone attacks in recent days, the US military said.

The strikes targeted "Iran-aligned terrorists that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) directed to attack US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement.

It further warned that "the IRGC and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response".

The CENTCOM statement did not mention the exact location it said Iran attempted to target.

Saudi Arabia confirmed its involvement in the strikes, with its defence ministry saying it hit "targets belonging to those militias present on Iraqi territory that are linked to attacks on the kingdom's oil facilities".

The strikes came after the ministry said its forces had intercepted drones targeting oil facilities in the east, blaming Iran-backed groups in Iraq.

Saudi Arabia called the previous day for the Iraqi government to prevent attacks from its territory, after which Iraq said it had ordered an investigation.

The IRGC later said they fired several ballistic missiles at a US air base and a US military CENTCOM centre in Jordan, in what they described as a response to US actions against Iranian interests.

US outlet Axios earlier reported, citing a US official, that Iran had launched ballistic missiles towards a US base in Jordan and the missiles were intercepted.

US President Donald Trump, who abruptly called off a two-week bombing campaign on Iran over the weekend, has said there were "good talks" underway with Iran but threatened to restart strikes unless negotiations delivered.

title.en: Japan quake toll rises to 13 as rescuers search for people trapped in collapsed mall
title.zh: 日本地震死亡人数升至13人，救援人员搜寻被困商场人员

summary.en: Rescuers in Japan are searching for people trapped after an earthquake struck, with the death toll rising to 13. The southern prefecture of Kumamoto has a history of devastating earthquakes, including a major one in 2016 that killed hundreds.
summary.zh: 日本救援人员正在搜寻地震中被困人员，死亡人数已升至13人。熊本县南部曾经历多次毁灭性地震，包括2016年造成数百人死亡的大地震。

body.en:
A 7.1-magnitude earthquake killed at least 13 people near the southern Japanese city of Kumamoto, and rescuers are frantically searching for survivors trapped beneath the rubble, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Wednesday.

"Even now, there are people waiting to be rescued, and this is a race against time. We will marshal all available resources on the ground to save and rescue as many people as possible," Takaichi told reporters at her office in Tokyo a day after the quake struck, raising the toll from three deaths reported earlier.

The quake knocked out power to thousands of homes and ruptured roads across the region.

Rescuers pulled eight people from the rubble of a partially collapsed shopping mall early on Wednesday. Two women in their 20s were killed as an apparent explosion of unknown origin ripped the mall apart about an hour after the earthquake.

Emergency fire rescue teams, police and army personnel were focusing on areas of the building where calls for help had been received.

Around 20 to 30 mall workers were unaccounted for on Tuesday, public broadcaster NHK said. Seven people are also missing after a chimney collapsed at a Nippon Paper Industries factory, while four others are seriously injured, a local government official said. Hospitals were reported to be treating dozens of patients.

Across the prefecture, which also suffered a deadly earthquake a decade ago, around 260,000 people were instructed to go to evacuation centres, authorities said.

The quake's epicentre was about 20km south of Kumamoto City, central Kyushu's largest city, with a population of around 700,000.

Authorities have warned residents in the areas that felt the biggest tremors to be on alert for further strong quakes for about a week, as well as for the risk of landslides.

With more than 36,000 homes still without power, authorities are worried about the risk of heat stroke as temperatures soar to around 34C on Wednesday.

One hospital in Uki city, near the epicentre, said a power outage caused by the earthquake meant it was unable to function.

"It's become like a field hospital," the head of the administrative department told NHK. Another hospital in the city said it had suspended admissions as it could no longer handle additional emergency cases after accepting 86 injured people following the quake, including three with serious injuries.

Several passengers aboard high-speed trains at the time of the quake were also injured, operators said.

body.en:
Spanish residents forced to flee some of the worst wildfires in living memory began returning to their homes on Wednesday, but thousands more were ordered to leave in France over fears that a looming heatwave would prevent containment of fires that have ripped through the country's southwest.

Swathes of tinder-dry forests, parched land and property have been destroyed west of the Spanish capital, Madrid, and in France's Gironde and Landes regions, forcing tens of thousands to head to safety.

Spain's interior ministry announced the end of evacuation orders for 13 municipalities on Tuesday afternoon local time, in rare good news for locals.

In the evacuated village of Navas del Rey, Reporters from the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency saw blackened debris, ash and burnt-out cars.

According to an initial estimate provided to AFP by municipal authorities, around 50 homes were destroyed by the flames and another 50 damaged.

Maria Paz Bolanos, 62, returned with her family to their home and garden in a housing development in the town — and found it only slightly scorched.

"We've been here 50 years," she said. "It must have been grandfather, my father in heaven. He somehow made it so the fire just came in through and stopped right there.

The mayor of nearby Pelayos de la Presa, Antonio Sin, described the scene as "a war zone".

"It has been a horrendous fire, a brutal one — it's a monster that has run over us," he told AFP.

In contrast, Marielle Mourgeon was among 4,000 people forced to cut short holidays in the French seaside village of Lacanau, in the Gironde area near Bordeaux, after camping sites were told to evacuate as a precaution.

"At first I thought my husband was joking, with the blue sky and the fires dying down," she said.

Over the past six days, the largest French wildfire since 1949 has raged west of Bordeaux , forcing more than 220,000 people to flee, destroying 240 houses and prompting questions about emergency preparedness.

Sophie Brocas, the government's top official in Gironde, told reporters the fire had "stabilised... meaning it is not advancing", and authorised nearly 60,000 people evacuated from three villages around the city to return.

South of Lege Cap Ferret on the Atlantic coast, volunteers have been working round the clock to help firefighters restock with water to tackle a wave of fires.

body.en:
The Trump administration has banned the import of humanoid and quadruped robots manufactured outside the United States, citing national security concerns. The ban could strain diplomatic tensions with China.

The United States has announced a ban on the import of foreign-made humanoid and quadruped robots in a move which will likely exclude Chinese manufacturers from the US market and could strain tensions between Washington and Beijing .

The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) said on Tuesday that "advanced robotic devices" produced abroad posed national and cyber security risks to the United States.

The decision was based on findings from a White House task force which concluded that foreign-built robots could create "a cybersecurity risk that threatens the security of critical infrastructure" and "the safety and security" of US residents.

The FCC defines the relevant mobile robots as devices weighing more than two kilograms that use sensors, network connectivity and software to achieve autonomous navigation, including the avoidance of obstacles.

The market for humanoid and quadruped (also known as four-legged "robot dogs") is seen as a major international growth area, with US and Chinese companies competing to develop the technology.

And China has a clear lead, with analysts at Barclays estimating that Chinese-made humanoid robots account for around 85% of the global market share. Morgan Stanley experts predict that China's humanoid robot market could be worth $15 billion (€13.2 billion) by 2030.

"Chinese manufacturers have been scaling production and reducing costs faster than most overseas competitors," Morningstar analyst Kangyuxiao Li told the Associated Press .

In the US, firms such as Figure AI are already deploying humanoid robots on production lines, while tech giant Tesla plans to begin production of its "Optimus" robot this year.

Currently, however, US robot exports remain in their hundreds while Unitree and AGIBOT, two of China's biggest advanced robotics companies, each shipped more than 5,000 humanoid robots in 2025 alone, according to the technology research and advisory group Omdia.

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the ban was also aimed at "secur[ing] America's critical supply chains."

But Li said the measures would not "materially slow China's overall humanoid development, given the size of its domestic manufacturing base and opportunities in other export markets."

Beyond the industrial market effects, the FCC ban could also have diplomatic consequences ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese Premier Xi Jinping in September.

title.en: Trump administration bans new Chinese humanoid robots
title.zh: 特朗普政府禁止新的中国类人机器人

summary.en: The United States has imposed a ban on new Chinese humanoid robots, intensifying the ongoing competition between the two nations to achieve global leadership in the fields of robotics and artificial intelligence.
summary.zh: 美国已禁止新的中国类人机器人，这加剧了两国在机器人和人工智能领域争夺全球领导地位的竞争。

body.en:
The Trump administration on Tuesday announced a ban on new foreign-made humanoid robot imports to the US over "unacceptable risks" to America's national security.

The move applies to advanced robots - including humanoid and four-legged machines. Many of them are made in China, which is competing with the US to develop robotics and artificial intelligence (AI).

The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) also banned imports of power inverters - devices used in data centres and solar panels - which it said could also pose a risk to the US economy.

The Chinese embassy in Washington said Beijing has long opposed the US' "politicising" of trade issues and sanctions based on "groundless pretexts".

FCC chairman Brendan Carr said the agency was doing its part "to secure America's critical supply chains".

The FCC has added the items to its Covered List - a register of goods and services that are deemed a risk to US national security.

The ban applies to new foreign-produced advanced robotic devices and power inverters and does not prevent the sale or import of any existing models that had been previously authorised by the FCC.

The FCC cited concerns that the use of foreign-made inverters could allow overseas firms to turn them off, steal data, facilitate remote access and surveillance by "foreign government actors, or be otherwise exploited through a cyberattack".

It added that the use of robots made outside the US could allow "malign actors to surveil Americans, enhance the capabilities of foreign intelligence services, or to remotely commandeer the robots".

The Chinese embassy in Washington also said Beijing will "take all necessary measures" in response to any moves that harm its interests, urging all countries to work together to develop AI "for the positive and for good".

It called on the US to "abandon its hegemonic mindset, and stop smearing Chinese companies and threatening them with sanctions".

The BBC has contacted major Chinese robot manufacturers Unitree, UBTech and AgiBot for comment.

China's exports have come under intense scrutiny by the US as the Trump administration attempts to address trade imbalances with the world's second largest economy.

Despite being the world's biggest exporter of electric vehicles, China has been effectively shut out of the American market by a steep tariff.

Washington has also blocked the sale of cutting-edge US semiconductors to China in a bid to protect national security, slow Beijing's military modernisation and maintain America's lead in AI.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has also warned that Chinese AI firms could face sanctions over allegations that they have stolen American intellectual property .

reflection.en: The global race to dominate advanced technologies like robotics and AI reflects a deep human drive to innovate and achieve. Yet, as humanity strives to build and lead, we are reminded of ancient stories where collective ambition, unchecked by wisdom, led to confusion rather than unity. Yahweh reminds us that true progress aligns with His purposes, not just...
reflection.zh: 全球争夺机器人和人工智能等先进技术主导权的竞赛，反映了人类创新和成就的深层驱动力。然而，当人类努力建造和领先时，我们被提醒古老的故事，其中集体野心若无智慧的约束，只会导致混乱而非合一。雅伟提醒我们，真正的进步是与祂的旨意相符，而非仅仅是人类对霸权的追求。

reflection.zh: 禁止某些先进技术，理由是存在“不可接受的风险”，这突显了在一个快速发展的世界中，远见和审慎的重要性。雅伟的智慧鼓励我们辨别潜在的危险并采取保护措施，而不是盲目冒进。这一原则不仅适用于国家安全，也适用于我们如何以关怀人类福祉的态度对待新创新。

title.en: Where Australia sits in this $6 billion race for influence as China's strategy shifts
title.zh: 澳大利亚在这场60亿美元的影响力竞争中处于何种位置，中国战略正在转变

summary.en: A new report indicates that China's strategic influence in the Pacific region, which was once significant, has recently diminished. This shift is noted amidst a broader competition for influence involving countries like Australia.
summary.zh: 一份新报告指出，中国在太平洋地区曾拥有的“真正立足点”已有所缩小。这一变化是在澳大利亚等国更广泛的地区影响力竞争中被观察到的。

body.en:
Australia has continued to outrank China as the Pacific's biggest source of development aid, contributing a third of loans and infrastructure investment to the region, according to a new report.

Looking at development projects across the Pacific between 2008 and 2024, the Lowy Institute report found that, after years of decline, aid to the region increased by 10 per cent in 2024.

Total development aid stood at US$4.1 billion ($5.85 billion) in that year, but the report's authors estimate that would drop to US$3.8 billion ($5.42 billion) in yet-to-be-released 2025 figures.

With China now shifting strategy from big debt-fuelled loans to smaller strategic aid, and amid major economic shocks in the Pacific, the contest for regional influence is coming under greater strain.

Australia was the Pacific's biggest donor in 2024, giving $2.14 billion in aid, which made up 37 per cent of all finance to the region in that year.

A total of $6 billion in financing was dispensed from New Zealand, China, and regional development banks.

Australia has also inked $3.4 billion in loan deals, ending China's reign as the region's leading lender.

"That's a product of many years of Australia pushing into these spaces, but it's meant that what was once a real foothold for China in the region has been narrowed," the report's lead author Riley Duke told SBS News.

"Australia is consistently providing the most grant financing to the region, and that picture hasn't really changed."

The report, released on Tuesday, says demand for Chinese loans has dropped since 2019 due to concerns about servicing the debt, more competition between lenders and Chinese banks' capital availability.

Australia is also a major financier of climate change mitigation projects in the Pacific, including a solar and battery storage facility for Palau to help generate 20 per cent of its electricity, and Tonga's Renewable Energy Stabilisation Package.

The fruits of those efforts have paid off for Australia, with a flurry of regional security deals announced in recent months, including with Fiji, Vanuatu , Papua New Guinea and Tuvalu.

"They are a clear marker of Australia establishing itself as the lead partner to the region," Duke said.

"Those deals ... take a long time to progress. They're complicated, but they reflect Australia establishing itself as an inalienably important partner to Pacific countries."

Developing Pacific Island nations have been hit hard by multiple shocks, including the COVID-19 pandemic and more recently, fuel supply shortages caused by the United States-Israeli war on Iran.

Duke said these multiple challenges put the region at risk of...
body.zh: 一份新报告显示，澳大利亚继续超过中国，成为太平洋地区最大的发展援助来源国，为该地区贡献了三分之一的贷款和基础设施投资。 洛伊研究所的报告审视了 2008 年至 2024 年间太平洋地区的发展项目，发现在经历了多年的下降之后，对该地区的援助在 2024 年增加了 10%。 该年的发展援助总额为 41 亿美元（58.5 亿美元），但报告作者估计，在尚未公布的 2025 年数据中，这一数字将降至 38 亿美元（54.2 亿美元）。 随着中国目前的战略从大规模债务驱动的贷款转向规模较小的战略援助，并且在太平洋地区遭受重大经济冲击的情况下，争夺地区影响力的竞争正面临更大的压力。 2024年，澳大利亚是太平洋地区最大的捐助国，提供了21.4亿美元的援助，占当年该地区所有资金的37%。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 新西兰、中国和地区开发银行总共提供了 60 亿美元的融资。 澳大利亚还签署了 34 亿美元的贷款协议，结束了中国作为该地区主要贷款国的统治地位。 该报告的主要作者莱利·杜克 (Riley Duke) 告诉 SBS 新闻：“这是澳大利亚多年来进军这些领域的结果，但这意味着中国在该地区曾经真正的立足点已经缩小。” “澳大利亚一直在向该地区提供最多的赠款融资，这种情况并没有真正改变。” 周二发布的报告称，自 2019 年以来，对中国贷款的需求有所下降，原因是对偿债的担忧、贷款机构之间的竞争加剧以及中资银行的可用资本。 澳大利亚还是太平洋地区气候变化减缓项目的主要资助者，其中包括为帕劳建设一个太阳能和电池存储设施，帮助其发电20%，以及汤加的可再生能源稳定计划。 这些努力的成果为澳大利亚带来了回报，近几个月宣布了一系列区域安全协议，其中包括与斐济、瓦努阿图、巴布亚新几内亚和图瓦卢的协议。 杜克说：“它们是澳大利亚确立其作为该地区主要合作伙伴地位的明显标志。” “这些协议……需要很长时间才能取得进展。它们很复杂，但它们反映了澳大利亚将自己确立为太平洋国家不可分割的重要合作伙伴。” 太平洋发展中岛国受到多重冲击的严重打击，包括新冠肺炎 (COVID-19) 大流行以及最近美国和以色列对伊朗的战争造成的燃料供应短缺。 杜克表示，这些多重挑战使该地区面临……的风险。

verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: The Guardian view on noise pollution: keep it down | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》关于噪音污染的观点：保持安静 | 社论

summary.en: New research indicates that noise pollution, particularly from traffic, has serious health repercussions, including a link to Parkinson's disease, affecting sleep and overall well-being.
summary.zh: 新研究表明，噪音污染，特别是交通噪音，对健康造成严重影响，包括与帕金森病相关联，从而影响睡眠和整体福祉。

body.en: New research linking the issue to Parkinson’s disease adds to the evidence of serious health repercussions from traffic volume and other sources The roar of late-night traffic is not just annoying for those trying to sleep. It can also have profound effects on their health. A pioneering new study, published this month, has found a clear link between road noise and Parkinson’s disease. The research, which followed more than 3 million Danish participants, found a modest but consistent effect: for every 11.5dB rise in noise level, the risk of the degenerative disorder rose by 3% over the 18-year study. The study adds to the growing body of evidence that auditory nuisance is associated with serious physical consequences. The European Environment Agency reported last year that more than 110 million people across the continent suffer high levels of health-damaging noise pollution, with physiological stress and sleep disturbance leading to 66,000 early deaths annually as well as heart disease, diabetes and depression. It found that the harm caused was greater than from secondhand tobacco smoke exposure. Continue reading...
body.zh: 将这一问题与帕金森病联系起来的新研究进一步证明了交通流量和其他来源对健康造成的严重影响深夜交通的轰鸣声不仅仅让那些想睡觉的人感到烦恼。它还会对他们的健康产生深远的影响。本月发表的一项开创性的新研究发现，道路噪音与帕金森病之间存在明显的联系。这项研究跟踪了超过 300 万丹麦参与者，发现了一个适度但一致的效果：在 18 年的研究中，噪音水平每上升 11.5 分贝，退行性疾病的风险就会增加 3%。这项研究进一步证明听觉困扰与严重的身体后果有关。欧洲环境署去年报告称，欧洲大陆有超过 1.1 亿人遭受严重损害健康的噪音污染，生理压力和睡眠障碍每年导致 66,000 人过早死亡，以及心脏病、糖尿病和抑郁症。研究发现，造成的危害比接触二手烟草烟雾造成的危害更大。您对本文提出的问题有什么看法吗？如果您想通过电子邮件提交最多 300 字的回复，以便考虑在我们的信件部分发布，请单击此处。继续阅读...

This includes considering how our collective actions, like traffic noise, affect...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻提醒我们，我们所处的环境，包括我们制造的声音，都深刻影响着人类的健康。创世记2:15呼召我们耕耘和看守雅伟赐予我们的世界，这一责任也延伸到为所有人营造和平健康的生活环境。这包括思考我们集体的行为，例如交通噪音，如何影响我们邻舍的福祉和更广阔的受造界。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.

verse.textZh: 知识是叫人自高自大，惟有爱心能造就人。

title.en: Britain promised to protect Hongkongers from China. Why does it now seem ready to sacrifice them? | Nathan Law
title.zh: 英国曾承诺保护香港人免受中国侵害，为何现在却似乎准备牺牲他们？| 罗冠聪

summary.en: Activists from Hong Kong, including former legislator Nathan Law, are facing unexpected challenges with UK immigration despite promises of protection. Concerns are rising that their safety might be compromised to foster better diplomatic relations with China.
summary.zh: 包括前立法会议员罗冠聪在内的香港活动人士，尽管英国曾承诺提供保护，但在英国移民方面却面临意想不到的困难。人们担心，他们的安全可能被牺牲，以换取与中国更友好的外交关系。

body.en: Activists under threat from Beijing are facing strange difficulties with UK immigration. Their safety must not be traded for warmer relations with China Nathan Law is a pro-democracy activist and former legislator from Hong Kong. He is currently a political refugee in the UK As authoritarian countries such as Russia, China and Iran are more active in engaging in long-arm strategies to silence their critics in the UK, transnational repression is garnering more attention. It is right that the Metropolitan police and other British law enforcement agencies have specific units and mechanisms to counter it. But it takes more than just confronting this long-distance repression to make political dissidents of these authoritarian countries feel safe in the UK, and the UK government is not living up to expectations. The threat is real. Members of the Hongkonger community have received threats from the Chinese regime – some have had threatening letters, some people were deepfaked into sexual content, some even had families questioned and arrested back home. With the level of this targeting linked to the deterioration of Hong Kong politics, many have utilised the humanitarian pathway enabled by the previous government to relocate. Continue reading...
body.zh: 受到北京威胁的活动人士在英国移民问题上面临着奇怪的困难。不能用他们的安全来换取与中国关系的缓和。罗冠聪是一位民主活动人士，也是香港前立法会议员。他目前是英国的政治难民。随着俄罗斯、中国和伊朗等独裁国家更加积极地采取长臂战略来压制英国的批评者，跨国镇压正在引起更多关注。伦敦警察厅和其他英国执法机构确实有专门的单位和机制来应对。但要让这些独裁国家的政治异见人士在英国感到安全，仅仅面对这种远程镇压是不够的，而英国政府并没有达到人们的期望。威胁是真实的。香港人社区的成员受到了来自中国政权的威胁——有些人收到了恐吓信，有些人被深度伪造色情内容，有些人甚至在国内遭到盘问和逮捕。由于这种目标的程度与香港政治的恶化有关，许多人利用前任政府允许的人道主义途径搬迁。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This situation reminds us of the biblical call to treat foreigners residing among us with the same care and respect as our own citizens. Yahweh's command to love the stranger, remembering our own vulnerability, challenges nations to uphold their commitments to those seeking refuge. It urges us to prioritize human dignity over political expediency.
reflection.zh: 这种情况提醒我们，圣经呼吁我们以对待本国公民的同样关怀和尊重来对待居住在我们中间的外国人。雅伟命令我们要爱寄居的，并记住我们自己也曾是寄居的，这挑战着各国要信守对寻求庇护者的承诺，敦促我们将人的尊严置于政治权宜之上。

The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.” Continue reading...

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

"A great degree [of its success] is due to the talent, infrastructure and the resources that were poured into building this...
body.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正在迅速缩小与美国同行的差距，引发了特朗普政府的新威胁。随着知识产权盗窃的指控，紧张局势会升级吗？ 似乎一眨眼的功夫，中国在顶级人工智能 (AI) 领域就从落后美国五年变为仅落后几个月。 尽管包括 Anthropic 的 Claude 和 OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 在内的美国企业已经花费了数千亿美元来推动人工智能的前沿发展，但中国却走了一条截然不同的道路。 面对美国对帮助人工智能实现最先进思维的高端芯片的限制，中国科技公司优先考虑了数十种基于“足够好”技术的开源人工智能模型。 这些平台，包括 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴的 Qwen 和小米的 MiMo，现已广泛部署在中国企业、政府服务和消费设备中。 作为缩小差距的最新迹象，中国初创公司 Moonshot AI 上周推出了 Kimi K3，该模型在关键基准测试上可与最先进的人工智能模型之一——Anthropic 的 Claude Fable 5 相媲美。 在某些测试中，Kimi K3 可以与 Claude 相媲美甚至超过 Claude，但其计算能力却要低得多，而成本却只是 Claude 的一小部分。 全球技术专家 Alvin W. Graylin 认为 Kimi K3 的到来将高端人工智能从昂贵的奢侈品变成了实用且负担得起的东西。 “对于 98% 的客户来说，[知识] 1% 到 2% 的差异并不值得多付 10 到 20 倍的费用。” 中国的最新进展已经引起华盛顿的强烈反应，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普现在威胁要阻止美国使用中国的人工智能模型。 与此同时，财政部长斯科特·贝森特本周早些时候警告称，美国可能会因涉嫌盗窃知识产权而制裁中国模型。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 指责中国实验室使用他们的模型来训练他们自己的系统，这一过程被称为蒸馏。 虽然提炼是全球人工智能实验室在一定程度上的常见做法，但这些公司表示，他们的模型已经受到查询的轰炸，以收获高级推理。白宫四月份警告说，中国正在以“工业规模”这样做。 北京方面予以反击，否认这些指控毫无根据，并称美国威胁实施制裁和示范禁令是“技术欺凌”，旨在遏制中国的崛起。 华盛顿智库史汀生中心战略远见中心的研究分析师朱莉娅·尼赫（Giulia Neaher）淡化了提炼在基米进步中的作用。 “[其成功]很大程度上归功于为建设这个项目而投入的人才、基础设施和资源......

body.en:
Claims that the federal government is using taxpayer money to bankroll media outlets for favourable coverage have spread online, sparking debate about press independence.

The Journalism Assistance Fund (JAF), launched last November, is a $67.6 million federal government program that subsidises the wages of more than 2,000 journalists at 185 news publishers across Australia.

Critics, including News24 (formerly known as Sky News) commentator Andrew Bolt, say the scheme could influence how outlets cover the government.

But the government says the fund is designed to support public-interest journalism, promote media diversity and help newsrooms navigate ongoing disruption across the media sector.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The JAF is a key part of the federal government's broader News Media Assistance Program, announced in 2024 and designed to support public-interest journalism and media diversity.

It provides grants to eligible Australian organisations that publish digital "core news content" that reports, investigates or explains issues relevant to informing democratic decision-making or current events of public significance.

Lifestyle, entertainment, celebrity, real estate and sponsored content are excluded, as are opinion and editorial pieces.

The grants subsidise part of the cost of employing full-time journalists, providing up to $13,000 per journalist each year, or $39,000 over the three-year life of the program.

According to the funding guidelines, the program aims to support Australian news publishers and the continued employment of journalists producing public-interest journalism.

The government says the scheme was in response to years of financial pressure on the news industry, as publishers face declining advertising revenue, newsroom closures and increasing competition from digital platforms such as Alphabet and Meta.

In a speech last week, Communications Minister Anika Wells said the fund was about sustaining public-interest journalism across Australia and rejected suggestions it could influence editorial decisions.

"This support is not conditional on what stories are written, and anything to the contrary is an insult to Australian journalists. Our media sector is strong and mature and I know they do and will continue to hold people to account, including those in government," she said.

The funding guidelines do not require outlets to acknowledge receipt of program funding, but state that, if an acknowledgement is included, it should state that the funding "does not influence the production of specific content".

body.en:
Share your feedback and help us improve this feature. Read more about how we use AI at SBS here.

What do you picture when you imagine a housemate? Someone younger or maybe a student in a cheap rental? Insight explores how the 'typical' share house identity has shifted, with more older Australians now finding themselves in house sharing situations. Watch Insight episode Housemates on SBS On Demand.

I usually have to do a mental headcount when people ask how many housemates I have. "Fifteen or 16, depending on the day" is my typical answer.

Often what follows is a look of disbelief and shocked statements like "I could never do that!"

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

It's also often followed by questions such as: "Isn't there so much conflict?" or "How does that even work?" or "Do you get any privacy?"

About three years ago now, when I was 19, I moved into the 16-person share house in Newcastle, about two hours north of Sydney.

I was living at home in a good location, and I got on well with my family; there was no reason I needed to move out.

But I was intrigued when a room in the big share house my two workmates lived in — and I had heard so much about — became available.

I had those same questions around conflict, lack of privacy — and I was nervous that many of the housemates were older than me. 

But one night, when the house hosted a winter solstice gig, convinced me to move in.

There must have been about a hundred people gathered around campfires in the backyard or dancing in the shed where a live band was performing. We shared home-cooked dhal for dinner and drank mulled wine and hot chai. 

The house, on a big double-block near the heart of the city, was started almost two decades ago by an environmentalist couple who wanted to use their inheritance to create and support sustainable, communal housing.

The house is just around the corner from my work. And sometimes, with a few of my colleagues who also live there, I go home to eat lunch.

We sit in the sun by the veggie patch — other housemates often stopping for a chat as they wheel their bikes into the bike shed.

One of the biggest joys of the home is our fully communal food. We all pay $45 per week to a food kitty and take turns doing the household shop at the local farmers' market and supermarket.

Cooking for a dozen people is a big undertaking and does take some getting used to. But the beauty of this cooking roster is that I only cook once a fortnight and I get to enjoy other people's home-cooked meals almost every other night of the week.

summary.en: Another interest rate hike in August is now seen as less likely.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An unexpected drop in Australia's inflation has eased fears of another imminent interest rate hike.

The latest Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) data showed headline inflation — the total inflation rate in an economy, including volatile items like fuel — falling from 4 per cent to 3.8 per cent in June.

It's now at its lowest level since 28 February, when the US and Israel launched an attack on Iran.

Trimmed mean inflation — which measures underlying inflation without volatile items and is the preferred measure by the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) — remained steady at 3.6 per cent, defying central bank predictions of a rise to 3.8 per cent.

The fall in inflation coincided with transport costs moderating for the month, ABS head of price statistics Rachel McCrick said.

"Lower world oil prices as a result of some stabilisation in the Middle East in June contributed to fuel prices falling 10.9 per cent in the month," she said on Wednesday.

"The federal government's fuel excise relief measures, which contributed to lower automatic fuel prices in April and May, also remained in place."

The fuel excise measures reduced the cost of fuel by 32 cents a litre during the month.

However, the measure was reduced to just 16 cents in July , and will be phased out entirely from Sunday.

Treasurer Jim Chalmers said the inflation figures were reassuring following a period of economic volatility.

"It's an encouraging outcome that shows we've made progress on inflation since the budget, even in the face of intense global uncertainty," he said.

"Treasury has warned that the next phase of the conflict could be more challenging for the global economy, with the oil market now more vulnerable."

Quarterly inflation numbers showed headline inflation falling from 4 to 3.9 per cent.

Meanwhile, the trimmed mean rose from 3.5 per cent in the March quarter to 3.6 per cent in the June quarter.

Housing remained the biggest contributor to inflation in the June monthly figures, rising by 6.8 per cent.

"Annual inflation for new dwellings has reached its highest level in almost three years, at 5.8 per cent," McCrick said.

The head of economic research at Oxford Economics Australia, Harry Murphy Cruise, said the RBA would be focused less on the headline figures and more on the breadth of price rises.

"Underlying inflation is not just resisting pressure to rise. In quarterly terms, it is continuing to ease," he said.

The RBA is due to meet on 10 and 11 August to decide whether interest rates will rise from current levels of 4.35 per cent, or keep them on hold.

summary.en: The NRMA is urging motorists not to panic ahead of the end of the fuel excise discount.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Treasurer Jim Chalmers has confirmed the fuel excise discount will end on Sunday 2 August, ending weeks of uncertainty over whether the discount would be extended for a second time.

"It was never the government's intention for [the discount] to be permanent," Chalmers said on Wednesday.

The initial discount of 32c per litre ended in June, after which the government extended the fuel excise cut at a reduced rate of 16c per litre.

"We began to taper that off at the start of the month, deliberately, so that we could provide a bit more cost of living help," Chalmers said.

While the NRMA does expect a modest rise in petrol prices from Monday, the roadside assistance and travel organisation doesn't expect costs to skyrocket.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"Our message to the public is: We know fuel prices are going to go up on Monday and beyond. We don't know by how much," NRMA spokesperson Peter Khoury told SBS News.

"We would expect average prices to go up a few cents per litre ... but it really depends on the service station."

The announcement ended weeks of uncertainty over whether the government would extend the fuel excise discount after Iran resumed its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, sending global oil markets into shock for the second time since the US-Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic in February.

Khoury said global oil markets were already responding to news on Monday that both sides had halted bombing , with benchmark unleaded prices dropping.

If the relative calm continues, Khoury said it will "definitely negate the increases we're going to get from the tax being reintroduced".

"We've seen a lot of restraint from the oil companies in the past few weeks," he said, adding that if global oil prices continued to fall it would "cushion the blow" of upcoming price rises in Australia.

Khoury said that price rises caused by the end of the fuel excise discount wouldn't happen overnight.

"Not every service station is going to put their price up by 17 cents a litre. In fact, almost none will. So please don't go out and panic buy."

Khoury told SBS News that, by the time the discount expires, it's likely the increase will be closer to 17 cents rather than the extended excise reduction rate of 16 cents.

"We think it's going to be another cent because of the inflation adjustment, which also just happens to land on the same day [Monday] they do that twice a year."

Just how much cost will be passed on to the consumer depends on individual service stations, Khoury added.

"We don't want people to panic because some service stations will go up on Monday and others won't; it really depends on when they sell their stock."

summary.en: A test flight successfully completed a 24-hour non-stop journey, marking a significant milestone in long-haul air travel. This achievement prompts questions about the future of traditional stopovers.
summary.zh: 一架测试航班成功完成了24小时不间断飞行，标志着长途航空旅行的一个重要里程碑。这一成就引发了人们对传统中途停留未来走向的思考。

body.en:
A record-breaking test flight lasting more than 24 hours has touched down in France from Melbourne — and experts say Australia could be leading the world on the new technology use.

Qantas' specially adapted Airbus A350-1000ULR landed in France on Tuesday after a marathon 24 hours and 24 minutes in the air, covering 23,057km without stopping — the longest direct flight ever attempted by a commercial aircraft.

The flight is part of a two-month test campaign as part of Qantas' Project Sunrise, which aims to launch the world's longest commercial passenger flight and reshape long-haul travel by offering direct flights from Australia's east coast to London and New York.

The previous record belonged to a Boeing 777-200LR, which flew 21,601.7km from Hong Kong to London in 22 hours and 42 minutes back in 2005.

Qantas has ordered 12 of the modified A350 aircraft, each fitted with an extra 20,000-litre fuel tank and configured to seat 238 passengers.

The first is due for delivery in April 2027, with daily non-stop flights between Sydney and London planned from October that year — turning what was once a five-day journey in 1947 on the old 'Kangaroo Route' into a single hop of 19 to 21 hours, depending on winds and routing.

The airline has said a Sydney-New York route will follow shortly after the launch of the London route.

The test flight's success has cast eyes towards the future of air travel, with some wondering whether stopovers in Singapore, Dubai or Los Angeles may be a thing of the past.

Justin Brownjohn from RMIT University's Aviation Academy says non-stop routes will keep becoming more viable as aircraft range improves and fuel use falls — but that doesn't make them a replacement for one-stop flying.

"Airlines have historically competed on network and frequency, but Project Sunrise competes on time," he said.

"Cutting up to four hours off the journey from Sydney to London and removing the connection entirely is a different product, not an improved version of the existing one.

Brownjohn expects the strongest demand for the ultra-long-haul services to come from business and premium leisure travellers willing to pay more for the time saved — and says the wider effect may be felt most by the Middle Eastern and Asian hub airports that have built their business models around the layover.

Spending over 20 hours in the air also raises real questions about passenger wellbeing.

"Twenty hours is not a longer flight, it is a different physiological event," Brownjohn said. "On this flight comfort has stopped being a luxury feature and become the thing being sold."
